en: 5. The Chapter on Truths (Saccayamaka) 5.3. The Section on Full Understanding (Pariññāvāra) 5.3.5.
The Section on the Present and Future (Paccuppannānāgatavāra)
Is it the case that whoever fully understands the truth of suffering will abandon the truth of the origin? No.
Or rather, is it the case that whoever will abandon the truth of the origin has already fully understood the truth of suffering? No.
Is it the case that whoever does not fully understand the truth of suffering will not abandon the truth of the origin?
Those who will attain the path do not fully understand the truth of suffering, yet they will not fail to abandon the truth of the origin.
Those who are arahants and those ordinary persons who will not attain the path neither fully understand the truth of suffering nor will they abandon the truth of the origin.
Or again, is it that whoever will not abandon the truth of origination (samudayasacca) does not fully understand the truth of suffering (dukkhasacca)?
One who possesses the highest path (aggamaggasamaṅgī) will not abandon the truth of origination, yet he does not fail to fully understand the truth of suffering.
An Arhat and those worldlings (puthujjana) who will not attain the path will neither abandon the truth of origination nor [fully understand] the truth of suffering.
And they do not fully understand the truth of suffering.
